utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Let the Registrar call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-00-39 and 40 PT, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik and Biljana Plavsic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. Your Honours, my name is Alan Tieger. I appear today with the Prosecutor, Madam Carla Del Ponte, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVICH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, Robert Pavich on behalf of Biljana Plavsic, accompanied by Mr. Eugene O'Sullivan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And there is a representative of the Serbian government; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BATIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am Dr. Vlatan Batic, Minister of Justice in the government of the Republic of Serbia, and I am appearing here at the request of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Dutch government are also here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DE MAN
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon. My name is Frederique de Man, Ministry of Foreign Affairs. I am accompanied by another colleague from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Mrs. Swaak, and Mr. Abraham Visser of the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. This is the adjourned hearing of a motion by the accused for provisional release. The principle of provisional release is not opposed. However, there is a dispute about where the accused should reside during the period of provisional release. Summarising the matter to date, the Prosecution do not oppose Mrs. Plavsic residing in the Netherlands, and the last hearing was adjourned for the Netherlands government to formulate conditions upon which such a release would be acceptable. Those conditions have been formulated and forwarded to the Court, and we have copies of them. The Defence now apply for Mrs. Plavsic to be released to reside in Serbia, and we have guarantees of that government relating to her travel arrangements, residence, reporting to police, and other matters. The Prosecution oppose this application, and it should be added that if it were not granted, the Defence do not oppose provisional release in the Netherlands on certain conditions. The dispute, therefore is as to where the accused should reside during a period of provisional release and that is the issue which the Court has to determine today. Mr. Pavich, we will begin with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVICH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would request at this time that we proceed, as we did on 1 August, in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It has emerged during the course of this hearing that there is no longer a dispute between the parties. The accused will be provisionally released to reside in the Republic of Serbia. The Trial Chamber makes that order now. There are a number of administrative details which have to be arranged. Consequently, a scheduling order will be made setting those out and setting out the date for the provisional release. It is the intention of the Trial Chamber that those should be accomplished as soon as possible. I should say we're grateful for the assistance of the representatives of the governments for coming and assisting the Trial Chamber. Court will rise.
